notes: Fourth sweep (2026-10-22-c, head 3e3581d): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. reads is empty in all five and no transcript has a Read or Skill call (tool calls are Write, Edit and Bash only); the only skill-file hit, references/palette.md, is in the listed dataviz skill's description, not a read. In the scratch folder all five compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.4); mix format --check-formatted passes for opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and fails for haiku-2 (line 12). Doctests: opus-1 (parse/1 @doc) and sonnet-2 (@moduledoc) have one example each, both pass. haiku-1 left check.exs (a smoke script that fails mix format) and an ebin/ folder in its run folder; they are not graded, as 2026-10-22 did not grade order-report opus-1's check.exs.

No graded rule changed since 0397dec: git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches the When to load it / Reviewing code bullets, Update structs (a defstruct field defaulting to nil is written as a bare atom), the do: rule (new sentences on do: bodies that mix format moves to their own line and on if ..., do:, else:), two new rules (Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call; Open a module with use, import, alias, require), Before you finish step 4, processes.md's ETS example and testing.md. None is in this case's list, so every verdict is graded to the 2026-10-22-b standard. Of the changed rules, only the do: rule's new sentence "The same holds for `if`: `if ..., do: ..., else: ...` fits when each branch is one short expression on the `if`'s line, and a branch `mix format` moves onto its own line gets `do ... end`." is broken, by opus-1 lines 225-227, recorded under other_violations. Every defstruct lists nil-default fields as bare atoms; every alias sits right after @moduledoc; the multi-line struct literals inside {:ok, ...} tuples are not call arguments and are not counted under the multi-line-argument rule.

Chain fallible steps with `with`, violating runs out of 5: one-step with 4 (opus-1 line 224, haiku-1 line 35, sonnet-1 line 170, sonnet-2 lines 216 and 220); else 2 (opus-1 fetch_timestamp/2, haiku-1 on its one-step with); case nested in a with body 0. sonnet-2's two are decided by "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step", since both bodies call normalize_currency/1; the others by the first sentence.

Naming, violating runs out of 5 per sentence: CamelCase/snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0; boolean ? 0 (not exercised); get/fetch 3 (opus-1 fetch/2 and five fetch_* helpers, sonnet-1 five, sonnet-2 fetch_data/1); size/length 0; ignored values 0; domain variable names 2 (sonnet-1 dt line 179, sonnet-2 dt line 126), held to the standard that flags dt; ts, raw, object, code, email, reason, type_string and parsed_data are not counted. data from the "data" key is allowed in every run.

Unchanged rules follow the previous sweeps' standard. A bare error -> error after {:ok, _} clauses (opus-1 lines 203, 219) counts under Match every expected shape, as 2026-10-21 counted baseline-haiku-1; _ -> {:error, {:invalid, key}} after a nil clause (sonnet-1) only receives present ill-typed values and is clean, as 2026-10-22-b graded opus-1's value -> clauses. Missing fields reported as invalid after Map.fetch (haiku-2) count only under Match every expected shape. haiku-1's from_data heads that match the data keys with a generic {:invalid_data, _} no-match clause are the shape the struct rule's second paragraph names and are clean under the struct and match rules, as 2026-10-22-b graded baseline-haiku-2; the unnamed fields go in checks. Keys bound in a multi-clause head and used only in the body are violations (opus-1 type_string, haiku-1 currency in Payment.from_data/2, sonnet-2 created); keys only guards use are clean. A public parse/1 without @doc (haiku-1, sonnet-1) counts under Comments; a section comment that says what the helpers below do (opus-1 line 189) counts as restating, as 2026-10-22 counted opus-1's "# Casts. Each returns ...". An if inside a with and a case inside a case go under Keep functions short in other_violations.

Borderline Read required keys call: opus-1 line 138 (defp event_type(type) when is_map_key(@event_types, type), do: {:ok, @event_types[type]}) reads a module-attribute map with brackets, but the guard on the same line has just checked the key, so the nil the rule warns about cannot occur; it is not counted. Counted, Opus would be violated on Read required keys.

Probe of 29 payloads in the scratch folder: every run returns an unsupported-type error for "invoice.paid" and reports a known type without amount as a field error, not as unsupported. opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 name every missing and invalid data field; opus-1 gives :invalid_payload for a missing type or data, sonnet-2 for a present non-string id or type, sonnet-1 names every top-level field too; sonnet-1 accepts "currency" => "EURO". haiku-1 reports every missing or invalid payment/refund field except currency as {:invalid_data, "payment"} / {:invalid_data, "refund"}, any top-level problem as :malformed_payload, and accepts "customer_email" => 5 and "failure_reason" => 5 unvalidated. haiku-2 reports every missing data field as {:invalid_field, key}, any top-level problem as :malformed_payload, and accepts "EURO" and "customer_email" => 5 (dropped to nil).

Compared with the 2026-10-22-b baseline: Opus moves from violated to clean on Read required keys (Map.fetch readers), from clean to violated on Match every expected shape (error -> error), the multi-clause rule (type_string in the head) and Comments (line 189), and stays violated on the with rule and Naming. Haiku moves from violated to clean on Read required keys and Naming, from clean to violated on the multi-clause rule (haiku-1's currency), and stays violated on Match every expected shape, the with rule and Comments. Sonnet moves from violated to clean on Match every expected shape and the struct rule, and stays violated on Read required keys (sonnet-1), the multi-clause rule, the with rule, Naming and Comments. Atoms, the return-tuple rule and (for Opus and Haiku) the struct rule stay clean in every tier.
